question: A hollow metallic sphere with an external radius of 10 cm and an internal radius of 6 cm is melted and recast into a solid cone with a base radius of 8 cm. What is the height of the cone? (Use pi = (22)/(7))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate volumes: Volume of Hollow Sphere = Volume of Cone

⇒ (4/3) × π × (R³ − r³) = (1/3) × π × r꜀ₒₙₑ² × h

⇒ 4 × (10³ − 6³) = 8² × h

⇒ 4 × (1000 − 216) = 64 × h

⇒ 4 × 784 = 64 × h ⇒ 784 = 16 × h

⇒ h = 49 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 49 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

External radius of sphere (R) = 10 cm

Internal radius of sphere (r) = 6 cm

Base radius of cone (r꜀) = 8 cm

Value of π = 22/7

 
• R=10 
• r=6 Hollow Sphere 
• 
 Recast 
 
• r=8 
• h=? Solid Cone 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of hollow sphere = (4/3) × π × (R³ − r³)

Volume of cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of hollow sphere = (4/3) × (22/7) × (10³ − 6³)

⇒ Volume of hollow sphere = (4/3) × (22/7) × (1000 − 216)

⇒ Volume of hollow sphere = (4/3) × (22/7) × 784

⇒ Volume of cone = (1/3) × (22/7) × 8² × h

⇒ (4/3) × (22/7) × 784 = (1/3) × (22/7) × 64 × h

⇒ 4 × 784 = 64 × h

⇒ 3136 = 64 × h

⇒ h = 3136 / 64

⇒ h = 49 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 49 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Solid Sphere

The volume of a solid sphere with radius r is given by V = (4/3) × π × r³.

Curved Surface Area of Cone

The curved surface area (CSA) of a cone is π × r × l, where l = √(r² + h²) is the slant height.

Total Surface Area of Hollow Sphere

The total surface area of a hollow sphere is the sum of inner and outer surface areas: 4 × π × (R² + r²).

Volume of Cylinder

A solid cylinder has a volume equal to π × r² × h, which is three times the volume of a cone with the same base and height.
